title: Onboarding field guide and signal sampler v0.3
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact field guide for new model entries into Redwood's serving catalog. It purposefully focuses on lightweight, repeatable eval steps, a small but representative prompt sampler, explicit success criteria (quant + qual), and a clear responsibility map so teams can move from exploratory validation to a safe canary rollout.

Scope / When to use this doc:
- For any externally trained model or checkpoint proposed for hosting (open weights, third-party provider model, or internally trained checkpoint) where we need to evaluate production readiness.
- Not a substitute for full security/compliance review for private deployments; those live in the security checklist linked below.

Quick summary checklist (single-page actionable):
1) Owner assigned and rotation: primary + reviewer (see Ownership Matrix).
2) Baseline smoke tests: compile + run inference w/ sample inputs under target seq lengths.
3) Prompt sampler run: run 250 examples across categories; collect metrics.
4) Latency & cost sweep: p95/p99 and tokens-per-second at target batch sizes.
5) Regression harness: compare to baseline model on holdout probes; surface diffs and examples.
6) Human QA pass: 30 spot checks covering hallucination, safety, instruction-following.
7) Rollout plan approved: canary thresholds + fallback policy.
8) Post-rollout monitoring plan defined (alerts + retention).

Ownership Matrix (minimal):
- Primary owner: Avery Chen (applied-ml) — owns the eval slate, data collection, and PR to registry.
- Secondary reviewer: Ravi Kapoor (serving-runtime) — validates runtime perf and kernel compatibility.
- SRE contact: Maya López (sre) — defines monitoring hooks and alerting.
- Product / stakeholder: Samir Desai (product-hosted-api) — approves quality bar for feature routes.

Model intake signals we collect (why each matters):
- Semantic accuracy (emb-sim and human spot-check) — measures factual/relevance.
- Instruction compliance rate (% responses that follow explicit instruction) — for instruction-style routes.
- Hallucination flag rate (human-labeled) — catches fabrications on factual prompts.
- Toxicity/threat rate (auto + human) — safety screening threshold.
- Latency p50/p95/p99 (end-to-end) — user experience SLOs.
- Cost tokens/sec & tokens-per-dollar — ops economics.

Prompt sampler design (250 probe slate):
- Composition: 60 classification-style probes (short), 80 instruction-following (medium), 50 summarization/long context (long), 30 few-shot code/formatting, 30 adversarial edge cases (truncated, prefix injection).
- Sourcing: mix of existing production prompts (anonymized), public benchmarks, and synthetic paraphrases.
- Sampling rules: preserve original intent; normalize user tokens by removing PII-only artifacts; keep deterministic seed for reproduction.
- Output capture: raw tokens, truncated flag, model-latency per token, tokenized length, attention to structured fields (if response should be JSON).

Quantitative success criteria (suggested thresholds; adjust per-route):
- Semantic similarity (avg embedding cosine vs. reference responses) >= 0.78 on instruction tests.
- Instruction compliance >= 92% on instruction suite.
- Hallucination rate <= 4% on factual QA probes (human-labeled sample of 200).
- Toxicity rate must be below 0.2% auto-detected OR be resolvable by prompt/control measures.
- Latency p95 <= 300ms for short prompts (under 128 tokens), p95 <= 800ms for long-context routes (>=1024 tokens).
- Cost per 1M tokens should not exceed X% of baseline model cost (set by product; placeholder 120%).
- Regression delta: No more than 1.5% drop in semantic similarity vs. baseline on holdout; any larger drop requires a root-cause + mitigation plan.

Qualitative checks (to capture nuance):
- Instruction sensitivity: does the model obey simple instructions like "Answer in 2 bullets"? Flag if repeatedly fails.
- Formatting fidelity: for structured outputs (JSON/my schema) ensure parse rate >= 98%.
- Tone consistency: spot-check for jarring style shifts that would harm user experience.

Regression reporting format (what to produce for stakeholders):
- One-pager summary: key numbers (similarity, compliance, hallucination, latency), pass/fail gates, short list of 10 representative failure examples.
- Diff artifact: side-by-side responses for each probe where delta exceeds threshold (store anonymized).
- CSV of metrics per probe and per-category.
- Human QA notes (30 checked): bullet list of issues, severity, suggested adjustments.

Instrumentation & reproducibility notes:
- Fix seeds for synthetic probes and save LR/decoder params used in sampling.
- Record model checkpoint id, tokenizer version, quantization flags, and runtime kernel variant.
- Push sampled traces to internal artifact store: path should include model:id/date/run-id.
- Preserve original prompts; never edit after an eval run except for normalization steps documented in metadata.

Rollout pattern (recommended):
- Canary stage 1: 0.5% of traffic for 24h. Automated checks: no alerts on latency, error rate, or quality regression on sampled set.
- Canary stage 2: 5% for 48h. Human QA gate: product + ML review of failure examples.
- Gradual ramp: 25% -> 60% -> 100% with at least 24h steady-state between steps.
- Fallback: always provide auto-fallback to baseline model variant; route-level circuit breaker tripped on any severe safety alert.

Monitoring and alerts to configure before rollout:
- Perf alerts: p95 latency increase >20% vs baseline OR p99 increase >15%.
- Quality alerts: sampled semantic similarity drop >1.2% OR hallucination increase >2x baseline.
- Safety alerts: toxicity spike >2x baseline OR any high-severity human label.
- Ops alerts: increase in OOMs or kernel errors >3 within 1h window.

Human-in-the-loop policy for early rollback:
- If any safety alert triggers, immediate rollback to baseline; SRE page and product pager.
- For quality regressions, pause ramp and trigger debug window (owners + reviewer) — 24h turnaround target for mitigation plan.

Small-section: common troubleshooting notes
- If p95 high but p50 unchanged: check batching and KV cache warm-up patterns.
- If hallucination increases after quantization: re-run with higher-precision kernel on sample failing probes.
- If formatting failures spike: compare tokenizer version and whitespace normalization.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Define exact cost cap (product to confirm).
- Decide whether to enforce a stricter hallucination threshold for finance/legal routed prompts.
- Need a short script to snapshot model metadata into artifact store (assigned owner: Ravi).

References & quick links:
- Confluence intake board: https://confluence.redwood.com/x/ABCD-portal-model-onboard
- Baseline model registry: github.com/redwood-inference/model-registry (internal)
- JIRA for this intake: JIRA-AI-2143
- Slack channel for run chatter: #applied-ml-onboard

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally lightweight; the goal is to reduce friction for good models while preventing common regressions that break product SLAs. Please add concrete metric changes if you think thresholds should be tighter for specific product routes.
- Suggest we run this workflow for the next three inbound checkpoints to validate that the sampler size (250) captures sufficient signal.
